title: Choose Pelican's visual world
question: The roll assigned The Mixtape. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Mixtape
options.lineage: home-taped cassettes, hand-lettered J-cards, index stickers
options.thesis: The watch holds 3.7 GB. That is not a disk, it is a tape — and you are making one for a run.
options.viewport: One continuous chassis. A capacity spool dominates the header — not a progress bar, a reel that fills as the tape does. Below it the tape's running order in hand-lettered rows, and a slot on the right where the watch sits, labelled with its own name.
options.risk: Skeuomorphic kitsch if it reaches for plastic textures and drop shadows. The commitment has to be to proportion, label typography, and capacity-as-the-organising-fact — not to a picture of a cassette.

raised.raise: The chassis owns the whole viewport as one continuous frame. No floating cards adrift on a background.
Every transfer state carries a written name. Colour never signals alone.
Anything temporary declares its own lifetime — a converted file says it is staged and when it goes.
A single strict grid module governs the entire surface. No ad-hoc spacing anywhere.
A hard-capped palette, with one colour reserved exclusively for alerts and never spent on decoration.

options.label: Quiet Utility
options.thesis: Disappear. The music is the content; the app is a pane of glass over a cable.
options.viewport: A single library list with album art at rest, a drop target that only appears when you drag, and a capacity strip in the toolbar.
options.risk: This is where almost every run in this category lands. It will look correct, ship fast, and be indistinguishable from any competent file-sync utility. Familiar and effective is a legitimate destination — but it is the safe one, and you rejected the last UI for being unremarkable.

options.label: The Gate Board
options.lineage: airport departure boards and segmented boarding passes
options.thesis: A transfer is a departure. Tracks are ranked by when they board, and a changed row moves in place and stays lit until you have noticed it.
options.viewport: The queue as a live board: each track a row with status, size and destination, reranking in place as the transfer advances.
options.case: Holds product clarity outright — it is the best answer anyone has to a slow serial queue with per-file states and silent firmware rejections that must stay visible. Loses audience identification: it frames a personal music library as logistics, and the curation half of the job goes cold. Competitive, not winning.
options.risk: Turns choosing music into operations work.

options.label: Starship Elbow Panel
options.case: Loses both axes. Numeric code clusters bury the one thing a user needs to read — the track name — and it is another sci-fi console skin, which is precisely the register just rejected.
options.kept: The frame itself is the layout grid.

options.label: Cyclorama Dawn
options.lineage: theatre lighting plots, black through cobalt to day
options.case: Loses both. Light gradients as state are ambiguous at a glance, and colour-as-signal fails the accessibility bar this build is meant to raise.

options.label: Cloud Quarry
options.case: Loses both, and badly. There is no honest mapping from quarrying weather to moving files down a cable, and inventing one would make the interface lie about the device.
options.kept: Temporary things announce how they end.

options.label: ASCII Live Render
options.case: Loses both. Phosphor-on-black is the terminal register the owner is moving away from, and glyph density is a hostile way to browse an album.
options.kept: One strict grid as the entire composition.

options.label: Teletext Service
options.case: Loses both for this audience. Three-digit page addressing is the wrong model for a file list, and the nostalgia is regionally narrow in a product meant for anyone with a Garmin.
options.kept: A tiny fixed palette, absolutely obeyed.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What a music-sync utility ships, executed impeccably: sidebar, list, toolbar, progress sheet.
canonCard.viewport: Source on the left, device on the right, transfer button between them.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from iTunes and every Android file manager, by design.
